$comment: MACHINE-READABLE ROSTER of the diagram engine. bd-09m6a, 2026-09-04. Generated by hand, VERIFIED by test/diagram_roster.js against the live registry on every run: the kinds, the aliases and the minimal_spec of every entry are asserted to render. Anything that consumes the type list -- the lp_doc schema enum, lint_lp.js, the author brief's SS4b.4 -- checks itself against THIS file, so the three can never drift from what the renderer actually supports. Prose home: reference/diagram_roster.md in the skill.

spec_conventions.lang: "ur" mirrors the layout and routes labels through a foreignObject with the Nastaliq stack. Formulae, chemical species, component values and axis numbers stay LTR even on an Urdu page. Urdu digits are U+06F0-06F9 (0123456789), never U+0660-0669.
spec_conventions.colour: A colour field takes a CSS colour STRING, and inside an lp_doc it must be a bare page token: var(--navy) var(--navy2) var(--amber) var(--amber-soft) var(--ink) var(--mut) var(--line) var(--leaf) var(--leaf-soft) var(--warn) var(--warn-soft) var(--warn-line). NO HEX FALLBACK -- lint_lp.js gate 10 harvests every string in the document and /#[0-9A-Fa-f]{6}/ is a hard PLACEHOLDER fail, so the var(--cool, #1B6CA8) form used by diagrams/examples/*.json is lint-fatal in a lesson. --cool --plum --clay --faint --teal are NOT lesson-page tokens and resolve to nothing.
spec_conventions.colour_exception: free_body.forces[].color is NOT a colour string. It is a short name looked up in free_body's own token map: ink | accent | leaf | warn | cool | clay. A var(--...) there falls through to the series cycle.
gates_every_diagram_must_clear: FIGURE  -- the smallest label renders >= 13.5px in the 750px full-width figure column (lint_lp.js).
DIAGRAM_OVERLAP -- checkOverlaps() returns zero colliding pairs. A hard fail, not a warning.
DEGENERATE -- checkDegenerate() finds no near-flat / zero-area shape.

types.for: One atom's electron shells, or the electron transfer/sharing between two atoms in a bond.
limits: mode is "bohr" (default) or "dot_cross" / "dot_and_cross"; using the dot_and_cross ALIAS as the type also selects that mode.
There is NO `compound` field. A bonding picture is element + partner + bond + transfer.
The built-in element table is H-Ca plus Fe/Cu/Zn/Br/I; anything else needs explicit Z/shells.

types.for: Three fixed biology schematics with leader-line labels: the plant/animal cell, the leaf cross-section, and the circulatory loop.
limits: kind is "plant" | "animal" and applies to type "cell" only; the leaf_cross_section and heart_loop aliases take no kind.
The structures are PARAMETRIC, not free-form -- you choose which parts are labelled, not what the drawing is. Anything else biological is a labelled_figure.

types.for: A balanced chemical equation typeset with real subscripts, charges, state symbols and arrow conditions.
limits: The equation is PLAIN TEXT, never \ce{}. Put spaces around any + that is an operator.

Arrows: -> <- <=> <-> = . A condition rides INSIDE the string as ->[Δ], and an equilibrium takes both: <=>[Fe][450 C]. There is NO top-level `above`/`below` field -- one written there is SILENTLY DROPPED and the arrow prints bare. The object form is conditions:{above,below}.
It does not check that the equation balances -- `balanced:false` only changes how it is drawn.

types.for: An IEC-symbol series or parallel circuit: battery, resistor, lamp, switch, ammeter, voltmeter.
limits: cells[].kind is battery | resistor | lamp | switch | ammeter | voltmeter. A voltmeter takes `across`.
Component VALUES stay LTR even on an Urdu page ("6 V", "10 O") -- that is how Pakistani textbooks set them. An Urdu value is now laid out correctly, but it is not the house style.

engine:"schemdraw" shells out to a Python venv that is NOT vendored into the serving repo; there it returns null and the built-in drawing is used, so a circuit looks different in NIETE than in an authoring run.

types.for: A depth-shaded double helix -- decorative on its own, or carrying a real base sequence with Watson-Crick paired, labelled rungs.
limits: kind resolves from spec.kind, else the alias used, else sniffed from the sequence (a U and no T reads as RNA), else "dna".
It is the HEAVIEST type on the page: ~30-45 kB of SVG against ~2-8 kB for everything else.
Two deliberate simplifications: no A-T(2) vs G-C(3) hydrogen-bond distinction, and the antiparallel 5'/3' property is named in the caption, not drawn.
NOT documented in the author brief SS4b.4 as of 2026-09-04, so a model working from the brief alone cannot choose it.

types.for: A SEQUENCE -- steps of a process, a chain of reasoning, a decision. If nothing happens first or last, it is a mindmap, not a flow.
limits: direction "lr" is the default and WRAPS into rows. "tb" stacks one column at ~150px a step: six tb steps measured 935px, 86% of an A4 page. visual_check V14 fails a tb flow of four or more steps.
Two short `lines` per step read; a paragraph in a step does not.

types.for: Part of a whole as a bar -- one fraction, an equivalence comparison on a shared whole, or a Singapore unit bar model with a total brace.
limits: Every bar is drawn to the SAME total width -- that is what makes a comparison honest, and it is why two bars with different `parts` are the right way to show equivalence.
Set urduDigits:true (or lang:"ur") for Urdu numerals in the labels.

types.for: The forces acting on one body, arrow lengths scaled by magnitude -- flat, or on an inclined plane.
limits: angle is in DEGREES with 90 = up.
forces[].color is a SHORT NAME (ink|accent|leaf|warn|cool|clay), not a colour string -- the one place in the engine where that is true.
body.shape "block_on_incline" plus incline.angle switches to the incline layout; decompose:true on a force splits it into components.

types.for: A shape, an angle or a construction -- triangles, polygons, circles with radius/diameter/chord/tangent, angle arcs, right-angle markers.
limits: The canvas AUTO-FITS the shapes; `height` is a hint, not a frame.
checkDegenerate() rejects a near-flat polygon, so give a triangle real area -- a 1-unit-tall 'triangle' fails the build even though it draws.

types.for: A relationship between two quantities -- sampled curves from a safe expression in x, plotted points, straight segments, and shaded half-planes for inequalities.
limits: functions[].expr is a SAFE expression string in x -- not JavaScript, not a lambda.

functions[].shade:"above"|"below" fills the half-plane on one side of the curve (PR #56). Two shaded functions overlap into a visibly darker region -- the right convention for a system of inequalities. Pair a strict inequality with dash:"6 4".
Shading covers only the curve's own VISIBLE x-range: if the curve leaves the window on the side opposite the shading, the region past that point is left blank.
points[].dx/dy are MANUAL label offsets. They can push a label onto an axis-tick plate and fail DIAGRAM_OVERLAP -- omit them unless you have looked at the render.

types.for: A percentage, a decimal, a fraction of a hundred square, or a multiplication area model.
limits: `shaded` is a COUNT of cells, filled in reading order -- not a list of coordinates.
majorEvery draws the heavier rule every N cells; 5 is what makes a hundred square countable.
A grid much past 10x10 stops being countable at a 750px column.

types.for: An HONEST PLACEHOLDER for decorative art this engine deliberately does not draw -- it prints the brief and a cache key instead of a blank box.

minimal_spec.brief: A flat-vector village scene at dusk: a raised water tank, a few houses, no people, no text.

limits: NEVER emit this inside a lesson plan. The author brief SS4b.1 rule 7 forbids it and it counts as ZERO toward the two-diagram floor -- it is a slot for a later art pass, not a visual.
Listed here only so the roster matches the registry.

types.for: A real textbook crop or photo whose callouts become REAL TEXT on leader lines -- the escape hatch for a structure no parametric type draws.
limits: labels[].at is [0-1, 0-1] in the IMAGE's own coordinates, origin top-left.
`image` is a data: URI or a filesystem path. It is the ONLY type that touches the filesystem; a path that does not resolve renders an error card that then fails DIAGRAM_OVERLAP.
The image is base64-embedded, so it dominates the SVG's weight (~120 kB for a 400px crop).

types.for: A whole broken into named parts -- a classification, the parts of a concept, the devices in a poem. NOT a sequence.
limits: Six branches read; twelve do not -- the canvas widens and every label shrinks toward the 13.5px floor.
Leaves are plain strings, not nested branches: this is one level deep by design.
Count the parts your objective names, then count the leaves. An objective saying THREE with a two-leaf branch is blocking defect B11.

types.for: A 2D structural formula from SMILES, with explicit-hydrogen sketches for the small hydrides and a formula card plus lattice for ionic compounds.
limits: A SMILES that will not parse degrades to the formula card; it never throws.
ionic:true (or a known ionic formula) draws the lattice instead of a structure -- NaCl is not a molecule and the drawing says so.
Give `formula` and `name` as well as `smiles`: the formula is what the pupil is examined on.

types.for: A position, an interval, a jump, or an inequality -- integers across zero, stacked fraction ticks, arcs for +/-, rays with open or closed ends.
limits: labelFormat is "integer" | "fraction" | "decimal"; a fraction line also wants `denominator`.
points[].style "dot" (closed, included) vs "open" (excluded) is the whole grammar of an inequality -- get it the right way round.
Too many ticks between `from` and `to` drives the labels under the 13.5px floor; raise `step` or `labelEvery`.

types.for: Two or three things set against each other -- evidence vs claim, before vs after, amanat vs khayanat.

panels.title: OXYGEN ATOMS
panels.sub: one O atom at a time

limits: TWO or THREE panels. A fourth squeezes every column under the legibility floor.
The panels are EQUAL width by design -- the point is that neither side is privileged.
`glyph` is one short symbol, not a sentence.

types.for: A monohybrid or dihybrid cross -- gametes, offspring and the genotype/phenotype ratios all COMPUTED from the two parental genotypes.
limits: DO NOT PRE-FILL THE SQUARE. The offspring cells and both ratios are derived; anything you type would be a second, disagreeing source of truth.
A dihybrid ("RrYy") gives a 4x4 grid -- readable, but it is the practical ceiling at a 750px column.
trait.dominantName / recessiveName may be Urdu; the allele letters stay Latin.

types.for: A lens or mirror construction SOLVED from the thin-lens/mirror equation -- F, 2F, the three standard rays, and the real or virtual image where it actually falls.
limits: element is convex_lens | concave_lens | concave_mirror | convex_mirror.
The image position, size and nature are COMPUTED -- you give the object, not the answer. u inside f gives the virtual case, and it draws that correctly.
It is the type that runs closest to the 13.5px floor (13.6px measured at full width): do not shrink its column.

types.for: Things that happened over time on a dated spine -- horizontal, or vertical chip-and-label for longer entries.
limits: FOUR TO SIX events, never more -- the brief's own rule, and past six the horizontal spine crowds its labels.
orientation "vertical" is the one to use when the labels are long; horizontal wants short ones.
The spine is EVENLY spaced, not scaled to the real intervals -- it shows order, not duration.
